FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.94  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.88  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` has no phase/ordering guard, so the same logical round can be processed repeatedly and later calls silently overwrite detector state while appending duplicate history elsewhere.** `ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings(round_idx, ...)` is keyed by `round_idx` and replaces prior data for that round, while `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round(...)` also overwrites by round index. In contrast, `RoleAssignment.record_failure()` appends, `FailureHandler` appends performance/failure history, and `DynamicManager._round_results` appends another `RoundResult`. This creates a non-idempotent split-brain state: convergence/diminishing-returns reflect only the last submission for round `r`, but failure history and audit history accumulate every submission. This is distinct from the already-noted duplicate index corruption in BLIND/SYNTH; it affects any repeated processing of an arbitrary round index and breaks replay safety, recovery, and auditability.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` does not validate temporal monotonicity of rounds, so callers can process future rounds before earlier ones and induce fabricated convergence/stop signals from implicit empty rounds.** `ConvergenceDetector.get_cumulative_classes(round_idx)` iterates `for r in range(round_idx + 1)` and treats missing rounds as empty; `DiminishingReturnsDetector` similarly accepts any `round_idx`. If the caller processes round 5 before rounds 1–4, the system computes cumulative/convergence over synthetic empty history, potentially concluding stability from absent evidence. This is broader than “future round_idx accepted” at the detector level: the orchestration layer never enforces that processed rounds form a contiguous prefix of the protocol.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.86  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` can permanently consume recovery side effects before discovering the round should have been terminal, because all failure handling is applied before any terminal-state guard or rollback.** The method mutates `_failure_history`, `_perf_history`, active-model exclusions, role-assignment failure history, convergence state, and diminishing-returns state before the FSM transition is selected. If later logic or callback failure aborts processing, there is no transaction boundary and no rollback. This is a deeper cross-cutting integrity issue beyond individual callback/event problems: orchestration is not atomic, so partial state commits are externally visible and can bias future scheduling.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.80  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`RoleAssignment.assign()` and `reassign()` can produce role maps containing zero `COL` even when multiple active workers remain, and `LoadBalancer` has no notion of synthesis/collation work that would force a collator to exist.** The code comments and architecture describe a distinct COL role, but load balancing only allocates generic `Task`s and ignores role-specific work classes. As a result, even if COL exists, nothing in the allocation layer ensures it does collator work; conversely in degraded pools the system can run without any COL and no subsystem notices. This is not just a stale-role issue already noted: the role architecture is semantically unbound from the task/allocation model, so an entire role can become performative metadata rather than an enforced operational responsibility.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.83  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager` never validates identifier consistency between `responses`, `findings`, and the active model set at the *round* level, so one malicious or buggy caller can cross-credit evidence across models without triggering any local inconsistency.** A benign `ModelResponse` for model A and a set of `Finding`s claiming model B are both accepted; failure handling evaluates A, while convergence/fingerprint updates credit B. Prior findings touched individual missing validations, but the deeper issue is systemic: there is no round-level evidence binding tying a response payload, extracted findings, and allocated/active identity into one integrity-checked unit.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION: 0.76  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The convergence and diminishing-returns subsystems use incompatible “newness” semantics, which can make the manager stop on a round that still improves cumulative yield under the convergence model.** Convergence novelty is class-based via `_novel_classes(round_idx)`, while diminishing returns is fed `new_findings_flat` obtained by flattening only those novel classes’ members. A round that meaningfully strengthens support multiplicity or aggregated severity of an existing class contributes to convergence evidence but is treated as zero novelty for the stop path. This is distinct from the already-reported duplicate-yield inflation bug: even after deduping, the two subsystems optimize different notions of progress and can disagree structurally.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.79  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.detect_failure()` and `get_recovery()` together encode a policy table, but `DynamicManager.process_round()` discards the chosen action except for `ABORT`, so the returned `RoundResult` is insufficient to reproduce or audit manager decisions.** `RoundResult.failures` stores only `FailureType`, not `RecoveryAction`, and `allocation` is always `None`. That means a downstream consumer cannot tell whether a model was retried, excluded, degraded, or merely logged, nor why the active set changed. This is deeper than “recovery actions are not executed”: even observability of the policy outcome is missing, so correctness cannot be audited post hoc.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.74  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.get_allocation()` can be called before any successful role/fingerprint synchronization after a failure-heavy round, yielding allocations based on a mixture of stale live fingerprints and newly changed active-model membership.** `FailureHandler` may exclude models during `process_round()`, and if the FSM becomes terminal or update logic is skipped, `_live_fingerprints` and role reassignment are not brought into a consistent post-round state. The next caller can still ask for allocations unless separately blocked. This is a cross-area state-consistency bug: active set, role map, and capability estimates do not have a guaranteed synchronization point.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.71  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` uses single-linkage clustering on a non-metric similarity function without any cluster-level consistency check, so classes can contain pairs of findings that are mutually below threshold and semantically far apart.** Because union-find links through bridges, if A≈B and B≈C, then A and C are forced into one class even when `sim(A,C) < tau_sim`. Prior findings noted cross-class merges and vocabulary sensitivity, but not this stronger consequence: the equivalence relation is not actually enforcing pairwise equivalence, so aggregated severity, novelty, and cumulative class counts can be driven by chaining artifacts rather than genuine class cohesion.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION: 0.69  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DiminishingReturnsDetector.smoothed_marginal_value()` silently drops infinite marginal values from zero-cost rounds, biasing the stop decision downward in exactly the cases where the implementation claims “free information always worth having.”** `marginal_value()` returns `inf` when `c_r <= epsilon_cost` and `delta_y > 0`, but `smoothed_marginal_value()` filters with `math.isfinite(mv)` and excludes those values entirely. If the recent window contains one highly valuable zero-cost round and one ordinary low-yield round, smoothing ignores the former and may stop early. This is a new semantic inconsistency beyond the previously noted `inf` pathologies.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.68  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.should_abort()` depends on `role_map` to identify the PM, but `role_map` is mutable shared state and can transiently diverge from `_active_models` and `models`; if PM identity is lost from the map, abort protection degrades to a weak cardinality check.** The code searches `role_map` for `Role.PM`; if none is found, it only checks `len(_active_models) < k_min`. In a corrupted/shared-mutation scenario, the system can continue with no identified PM as long as enough models remain active. This is a deeper invariant hole than the already-reported shared-dict mutability: the PM safety guarantee is not defended by an immutable source of truth.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.66  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The event protocol is not causally ordered with manager state transitions, so observers cannot reliably infer whether an emitted event describes pre-state, in-flight state, or committed post-state.** For example, `CONVERGENCE_CHECK` and `STOP_CHECK` are emitted before FSM transition, `ROUND_COMPLETE` is emitted before processing begins, and another `ROUND_COMPLETE` is emitted after fingerprint updates. Even without callback failures, external control logic consuming the stream cannot build a consistent state machine from events alone. This is broader than duplicate/misnamed event issues: the monitoring interface lacks a coherent causal contract.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.60  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManagementConfig.get_alpha()` and `get_baseline()` silently default any non-PM/non-COL role value to PAR rather than rejecting invalid input.** Because the methods use `else: return par`, any accidental foreign enum, mocked role object, or corrupted value routes to participant coefficients without error. In a system whose behavior is strongly role-dependent, silent fallback masks invariant violations and produces hard-to-debug mis-scoring rather than failing fast.

FINDING_ID: ROUND10_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.58  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The public dataclasses (`CapabilityFingerprint`, `ModelSpec`, `Task`, `Finding`, `ModelResponse`) have no invariant enforcement and are consumed by arithmetic paths that assume finite numeric domains, enabling silent NaN propagation across nearly every subsystem.** Some prior findings mentioned non-finite values in isolated places, but the broader missed issue is architectural: there is no ingress validation boundary anywhere. A single NaN in `Finding.severity`, `Task.token_demand`, `ModelSpec.tau`, or `CapabilityFingerprint` can contaminate ranking, feasibility, convergence, yield, and event metadata without a unified guardrail.
